title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea — Muziris, Nelkynda and the Limyrike coast (§53-56)
language_note: Original Greek, anonymous 1st-century merchant's sailing manual (same work as arabia-01-periplus, different section).
original_text_excerpt:
53. Μετὰ δὲ Καλλίεναν ἄλλα ἐμπόρια τοπικὰ Σήμυλλα καὶ Μανδαγόρα καὶ Παλαιπάτμαι καὶ Μελιζειγάρα καὶ Βυζάντιον καὶ Τοπαρὸν καὶ Τυραννοσβόας. Εἶτα Σησεκρείεναι λεγόμεναι νῆσοι καὶ ἡ τῶν Αἰγιδίων καὶ ἡ τῶν Καινειτῶν κατὰ τὴν λεγομένην Χερσόνησον, καθ᾽ οὓς τόπους εἰσὶ πειραταὶ, καὶ μετὰ ταύτην Λευκὴ νῆσος. Εἶτα Νάουρα καὶ Τύνδις τὰ πρῶτα ἐμπόρια τῆς Λιμυρικῆς, καὶ μετὰ ταύτας Μουζιρὶς καὶ Νέλκυνδα, αἱ νῦν πράσσουσαι.

54. Βασιλείας δ᾽ ἐστὶν ἡ μὲν Τύνδις Κηπροβότρου, κώμη παραθαλάσσιος ἔνσημος· ἡ δὲ Μουζιρὶς βασιλείας μὲν τῆς αὐτῆς, ἀκμάζουσα δὲ τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀριακῆς εἰς αὐτὴν ἐρχομένοις πλοίοις καὶ τοῖς Ἑλληνικοῖς· κεῖται δὲ παρὰ ποταμὸν, ἀπέχουσα ἀπὸ μὲν Τύνδεως διὰ τοῦ ποταμοῦ καὶ διὰ θαλάσσης σταδίους πεντακοσίους, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ κατ᾽ αὐτὴν εἴκοσι. Ἡ δὲ Νέλκυνδα σταδίους μὲν ἀπὸ Μουζιρέως ἀπέχει σχεδὸν πεντακοσίους, ὁμοίως διά τε ποταμοῦ καὶ πεζῇ καὶ διὰ θαλάσσης, βασιλείας δέ ἐστιν ἑτέρας, τῆς Πανδίονος· κεῖται δὲ καὶ αὐτὴ παρὰ ποταμὸν, ὡσεὶ ἀπὸ σταδίων ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι τῆς θαλάσσης.

55. Ἑτέρα δὲ κατ᾽ αὐτὸ τὸ στόμα τοῦ ποταμοῦ πρόκειται κώμη Βακαρὴ, εἰς ἣν ἀπὸ Νελκύνδων ἐπὶ τῆς ἀναγωγῆς προκαταβαίνουσι τὰ πλοῖα καὶ ἐπὶ σάλου διορμίζεται πρὸς ἀνάληψιν τῶν φορτίων διὰ δὴ τὸν ποταμὸν ἕρματα καὶ διάπλους ἔχειν ἐλαφρούς. Αὐτοὶ δὲ οἱ βασιλεῖς ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἐμπορίων ἐν τῇ μεσογείᾳ κατοικοῦσι. Καὶ περὶ τούσδε τοὺς τόπους τοῖς ἐκ πελάγους ἐρχομένοις σημεῖον ἐπιβολῆς εἰσιν οἱ προαπαντῶντες ὄφεις, μέλανες μὲν καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν χρόαν, βραχύτεροι δὲ καὶ δρακοντοειδεῖς τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τοῖς ὄμμασιν αἱματώδεις.

56. Πλεῖ δὲ εἰς τὰ ἐμπόρια ταῦτα μεγάλα πλοῖα διὰ τὸν ὄγκον καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ πεπέρεως καὶ τοῦ μαλαβάθρου. Προχωρεῖ δὲ εἰς αὐτὴν προηγουμένως χρήματα πλεῖστα, χρυσόλιθα, ἱματισμὸς ἁπλοῦς οὐ πολὺς, πολύμιτα, στίμμι, κοράλλιον, ὕαλος ἀργὴ, χαλκὸς, κασσίτερος, μόλυβδος, οἶνος οὐ πολὺς, ὡσεὶ δὲ τοσοῦτον ὅσον ἐν Βαρυγάζοις, σανδαράκη, ἀρσενικὸν, σῖτος δὲ ὅσος ἀρκέσει τοῖς περὶ τὸ ναυκλήριον διὰ τὸ μὴ τοὺς ἐμπόρους αὐτῷ χρῆσθαι. Φέρεται δὲ πέπερι μονογενῶς ἐν ἑνὶ τόπῳ τούτων τῶν ἐμπορίων γεννώμενον πολὺ, τῇ λεγομένῃ Κοττοναρικῇ· φέρεται δὲ καὶ μαργαρίτης ἱκανὸς καὶ διάφορος καὶ ἐλέφας καὶ ὀθόνια Σηρικὰ καὶ νάρδος ἡ Γαγγητικὴ καὶ μαλάβαθρον ἐκ τῶν ἔσω τόπων εἰς αὐτὴν, καὶ λιθία διαφανὴς παντοία καὶ ἀδάμας καὶ ὑάκινθος καὶ χελώνη ἥ τε Χρυσονησιωτικὴ καὶ ἡ περὶ τὰς νήσους θηρευομένη τὰς προκειμένας αὐτῆς τῆς Λιμυρικῆς. Πλέουσι δὲ εἰς αὐτὴν οἱ κατὰ καιρὸν ἀναγόμενοι ἀπ᾽ Αἰγύπτου περὶ τὸν Ἰούλιον μῆνα, ὅ ἐστιν Ἐπιφί.
original_text_note: Verbatim Koine Greek recovered 2026-08-09 from the Greek Wikisource text of C. Müller, Geographi Graeci Minores I (Paris 1855), which is in the public domain. Section numbers (§) are Müller's and are retained in the text so the chunker can split on them. Marginal sigla and editorial asterisks in the Wikisource copy have been omitted; wording is otherwise unaltered. Extended 2026-08-09 from §53-54 to §53-56: §56 carries the cargo manifest (pepper from Kottanarike, Gangetic nard, ivory, Chinese silk cloth, pearls, diamonds) and the July sailing season from Egypt — the passage that actually documents Roman trade at the port. §55 is included to keep the excerpt contiguous. RESOLVED 2026-08-10: reference_translation now carries Schoff's §53-56 in full, so original and translation cover the same sections again — see reference_translation_note. RECOVERY 2026-08-13: the excerpt held on disk was found to be 91.3% of this section range as the cited Wikisource text gives it — 210 characters of Koine Greek missing across 1 sections, dropped silently and not recorded by the note above, which described only the wording of what was present. Restored in full from the same source and the same edition, with the same normalisation applied as on 2026-08-09: editorial brackets and parentheses removed and their contents kept, asterisk sigla removed, runs of whitespace collapsed, and Müller's section numbers retained so the chunker can still split on them. No word is altered, added or reordered. Found while extracting subject places for Phase 2 A4: places named in the reference translation had no counterpart in the original — see PROGRESS.md.
reference_translation:
53. Beyond Calliena there are other market-towns of this region; Semylla, Mandagora, Pala patma, Meligara, Byzantium, Togarum and Aurannohoas. Then there are the islands called Sesecrienae and that of the Aegidii, and that of the Caenitae, opposite the place called Chersonesus (and in these places there are pirates) and after this the White Island. Then come Naura and Tyndis, the first markets of Damirica, and then Muziris and Nelcynda, which are now of leading importance.

54. Tyndis is of the Kingdom of Cerobothra; it is a village in plain sight by the sea. Muziris, of the same Kingdom, abounds in ships sent there with cargoes from Arabia, and by the Greeks; it is located on a river, distant from Tyndis by river and sea five hundred stadia, and up the river from the shore twenty stadia. Nelcynda is distant from Muziris by river and sea about five hundred stadia, and is of another Kingdom, the Pandian. This place also is situated on a river, about one hundred and twenty stadia from the sea.

55. There is another place at the mouth of this river, the village of Bacare; to which ships drop down on the outward voyage from Nelcynda, and anchor in the roadstead to take on their cargoes; because the river is full of shoals and the channels are not clear. The kings of both these market-towns live in the interior. And as a sign to those approaching these places from the sea there are serpents coming forth to meet you, black in color, but shorter, like snakes in the head, and with blood-red eyes.

56. They send large ships to these market-towns on account of the great quantity and bulk of pepper and malabathrum. There are imported here, in the first place, a great quantity of coin; topaz, thin clothing, not much; figured linens, antimony, coral, crude glass, copper, tin, lead; wine, not much, but as much as at Barygaza; realgar and orpiment; and wheat enough for the sailors, for this is not dealt in by the merchants there. There is exported pepper, which is produced in quantity in only one region near these markets, a district called Cottonara. Besides this there are exported great quantities of fine pearls, ivory, silk cloth, spikenard from the Ganges, malabathrum from the places in the interior, transparent stones of all kinds, diamonds and sapphires, and tortoise-shell; that from Chryse Island, and that taken among the islands along the coast of Damirica. They make the voyage to this place in a favorable season who set out from Egypt about the month of July, that is Epiphi.
translation_source: Wilfred H. Schoff translation (1912), University of Washington Silk Road Seattle hosted edition.
reference_translation_note: Extended 2026-08-10 from a partial, elided excerpt of §53-54 to the full §53-56, so that the reference translation covers the same sections as original_text_excerpt. Taken verbatim from the Silk Road Seattle digitisation of Wilfred H. Schoff, The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (New York 1912), which is out of copyright. Two classes of change, both mechanical: (1) the modern editors' square-bracket glosses comparing Casson's readings (e.g. 'Damirica [=Limyrike]') are omitted, so the field holds Schoff's own wording and nothing else; (2) one line-break hyphenation artefact of the digitisation ('ex-ported') is closed up. Schoff's place-name spellings are left exactly as digitised, including 'Pala patma' and 'Aurannohoas', rather than silently emended — an editorial correction here would be indistinguishable from source wording downstream. Section numbers added to mirror the Greek so the two sides split at the same boundaries. This record is the corpus's primary back-translation test case (Part 6): four Greek sections with published English to score machine translation against.

notes: Direct external (Roman-Greek) corroboration of the Akananuru 149 and Pattanam excavation evidence (southasia-01, southasia-04) for the same port — an excellent triangulation case for the knowledge graph phase (Pillar 2): three independent source types (Tamil poem, Greek sailing manual, archaeological find record) converging on one place, Muziris. Coverage is symmetric as of 2026-08-10: original and reference translation both cover §53-56 (Greek from Müller 1855, English from Schoff 1912). That symmetry is what makes this the corpus's best back-translation gold case in Part 6.

subject_places.name: Muziris
subject_places.note: 50146 Muziris 10.154/76.213, 'settlement, port', -30..640, locationPrecision 'precise'. That coordinate IS Pattanam. Pleiades has therefore already adopted the identification `southasia-04-pattanam` treats as open, and marks it precise; read that record's findspot note before changing this one. What is contested there is whether the excavation site is Muziris — a claim about the coordinate. What this record does is name the place, which is why the ground here is 'stated' and the contested flag is not repeated: per PLACES.md, contested belongs to an identification, not to the fact that a text names a place.

subject_places.name: Calliena
subject_places.note: 50023 Kalliena 19.273/73.139, settlement, -30..640 — Kalyan, near Mumbai. §53's list of market-towns begins from it.

subject_places.name: Semylla
subject_places.note: 50261 Semylla 18.521/72.947, settlement, -30..300 — the Konkan coast.

subject_places.name: Mandagora
subject_places.note: 50116 'Mandagara?' 17.951/73.039, settlement, -30..300. Pleiades' own query mark is retained in its title and is its uncertainty, not ours.

subject_places.name: Melizeigara
subject_places.note: §53's Μελιζειγάρα. No entry in Pleiades under any form searched; one of the Konkan market-towns that has never been located.

subject_places.name: Byzantion
subject_places.note: **Not Constantinople.** 49929 'Byzantion?' 16.503/73.340, settlement, -30..300 — a market-town on the Konkan coast, in §53's list between Melizeigara and Toparon. The case where accepting an id on its coordinate rather than its name pays for the whole rule.

subject_places.name: Toparon
subject_places.note: 50308 'Toparon?' 16.220/73.585, settlement, -30..300. The Greek reads Τοπαρόν; Schoff prints 'Togarum', which resolves to nothing — the placement follows the original.

subject_places.name: Tyrannosboas
subject_places.note: 50315 'Tyrannosboas?' 16.079/73.472, settlement, -30..300. Greek Τυραννοσβόας against Schoff's 'Aurannohoas', which resolves to nothing.

subject_places.name: the Sesecrienae islands
subject_places.note: 50264 'Sesekreienai? Inss.' 17.500/72.500, 'archipelago, label', locationPrecision 'rough'.

subject_places.name: the island of the Caenitae
subject_places.note: 50015 'Kaineiton Nesos' 12.500/72.500, island, locationPrecision 'rough'.

subject_places.name: Chersonesus
subject_places.note: §53's Χερσόνησος, on the Konkan. Twenty-three entries carry the name and every one is Black Sea, Aegean, Libyan or Thracian; none is Indian. Refused rather than resolved to a Greek peninsula.

subject_places.name: the White Island
subject_places.note: §53's Λευκὴ νῆσος. 50091 'Leuke (island)' 14.019/74.325, island, -30..2100 — the Karnataka coast. Found only on a description match; a title search returns 226677 'Leuke Ins./Achilleos Nesos' at 45.255/30.204, which is Snake Island in the **Black Sea**, and which is refused.

subject_places.name: Naura
subject_places.note: 50160 'Naoura/Nitriae' 14.281/74.450, settlement, -30..300 — §53 makes it one of the first two markets of Limyrike, on the way down the coast to Muziris. Refused: 638923 Kitanaura, in Lycia.

subject_places.name: Tyndis
subject_places.note: 50312 Tyndis 10.764/75.926, settlement, -30..300 — the Kerala coast, §54's 500 stadia from Muziris. Refused: 50313 'Tyndis (river)' at 22.500/82.500, 'rough', which shares the name and is inland.

subject_places.name: Nelcynda
subject_places.note: 50165 Nelkynda 9.273/76.559, settlement, -30..300 — §54 puts it ~500 stadia from Muziris and in the other kingdom, the Pandian.

subject_places.name: Bacare
subject_places.note: §55's village at the river mouth where ships drop down to take on cargo. 49890 Bakare 9.351/76.368, 'settlement, settlement-modern', -30..2099. **Refused: 785982 'Bakare'**, an Egyptian mine at 25.210/34.274 — the same name, the wrong continent.

subject_places.name: the Kingdom of Cerobothra
subject_places.note: §54's βασιλεία Κηπροβότρου, the Chera kingdom, to which Tyndis and Muziris both belong. Nothing resolves: 246333 'Chera' is a settlement in Spain and is refused; the other hits are Italian and Anatolian.

subject_places.name: the Kingdom of the Pandion
subject_places.note: §54's βασιλεία τῆς Πανδίονος, Nelkynda's kingdom. 50201 Pandion 9.654/78.194, label, -330..640 — the Pandya country around Madurai. Refused: 599854 'Pandion Collis', a mountain in Caria.

subject_places.name: Limyrike
subject_places.note: §53 and §56's Λιμυρική. 50092 Limyrike 11.072/75.922, label, -30..300. **Schoff prints 'Damirica' throughout**, which resolves to nothing; the placement follows the Greek.

subject_places.name: Ariake
subject_places.note: §54: ἀκμάζουσα τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀριακῆς εἰς αὐτὴν ἐρχομένοις πλοίοις — Muziris thrives on the ships that come to it FROM ARIAKE. **Schoff prints 'from Arabia' here**, and Arabia is a thousand miles from the Konkan; this entry is the reason the standing rule is that a placement follows the original and not the reference translation. Two ids were examined and neither is used: 59700 'Ariake/Larike' 22.304/71.976, the Saurashtra label, and 49874 'Ariake Sadenon' 18.143/74.499, inland Maharashtra. The Periplus's Ariake spans the coast between them (cf. §41, where it adjoins Barygaza, and §14), so either id would assert a narrower place than the text does. Regional, and the map is sparser.

subject_places.name: Barygaza
subject_places.note: 59737 Barygaza 21.701/72.983, settlement, -330..2099 — Bharuch on the Gulf of Khambhat. §56 uses it only as the measure of how much wine is imported — 'as much as at Barygaza'. A comparison, so no edge.

subject_places.name: Cottonara
subject_places.note: §56: pepper is produced in one region only, τῇ λεγομένῃ Κοττοναρικῇ. 49953 Cottonara 9.004/76.889, 'district, label', -30..300.

subject_places.name: the Ganges
subject_places.note: §56's νάρδος ἡ Γαγγητική, spikenard from the Ganges. 59822 'Ganges (river)' 25.932/83.780, river, -330..2100. **Refused: 49984**, which carries the name 'Ganges' and is a river in **Sri Lanka**.

subject_places.name: Chryse
subject_places.note: §56's tortoise-shell ἥ τε Χρυσονησιωτική, from Chryse Island. Both candidates resolve and are UNLOCATED — 60485 'Chryse/Aurea' and 50630 'Chrysei' — so neither carries a coordinate. The Aegean and Anatolian Chryses are refused on coordinate. A6's `unlocated` key deliberately NOT used here: it takes one id, and which of the two this is has never been decided. Kyeneion and Sabbatha each had a single candidate and now cite it; this one is a curation question first, and recording either id would settle by keystroke a question nobody has settled by argument.

subject_places.name: Egypt
subject_places.note: 766 'Aegyptus (Roman imperial province)', locationPrecision 'related', attested -30..2100 — contemporary with the Periplus, which is why it is used where Pleiades 837 'Asia Minor' was refused for persia-02 (that one is attested 1700..1799, a modern cartographic label). Its representative point 31.201/29.910 is Alexandria's own coordinate, so this placement must render as an extent and never as a pin; see `has_area` in gazetteer.py.
